cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Maternal – Relating to a mother, especially in showing affection or instinct.

p.em: Example: Rebecca's sudden maternal urge was less about love and more about proving a point.

cosy-blockquote.p: Overzealous – Too zealous; overly enthusiastic and aggressive in pursuit of a goal.

p.em: Example: An overzealous babysitter can turn a peaceful afternoon into a military exercise.

cosy-blockquote.p: Compulsive – Resulting from or acting on an irresistible urge or impulse.

p.em: Example: Her compulsive need to fix other people's lives masked her own chaos.

cosy-blockquote.p: Harrowing – Acutely distressing, painful, or terrifying.

p.em: Example: Babysitting a toddler proved to be a far more harrowing ordeal than expected.

cosy-blockquote.p: Matriarch – A woman who is the head of a family, group, or organizational hierarchy.

p.em: Example: She strutted into the nursery acting like an ancient, all-knowing matriarch.

cosy-blockquote.p: Expectations – Strong beliefs that something will or should happen in a certain way.

p.em: Example: Unrealistic parenting expectations generate endless unnecessary guilt.

cosy-blockquote.p: Instinctual – Relating to or prompted by natural impulse rather than training.

p.em: Example: She claimed her aggressive childcare methods were purely instinctual.

cosy-blockquote.p: Tireless – Capable of working or continuing for a long time without fatigue.

p.em: Example: Her tireless devotion to organic gluten-free snacks exhausted everyone.

cosy-blockquote.p: Raising – The process of bringing up and educating a child.

p.em: Example: Raising kids requires patience rather than performative perfection.

cosy-blockquote.p: Perfect – Free from all flaws or defects; ideal in every way.

p.em: Example: Trying to appear like a perfect parent online is a recipe for burnout.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Share whether you agree or disagree with these statements and discuss them with your teacher:

ul.li: Incorrect: She is so maternal than her sister → Correct: She is more maternal than her sister ((Use 'more... than' for comparative adjectives, reserve 'so' for intensity without 'than'.))
Incorrect: She is good in raising kids → Correct: She is good at raising kids ((Use 'good at' when expressing skill or competence.))
Incorrect: They have high expectations for the child → Correct: They have high expectations of the child ((Use 'expectations of' someone.))
